I think by now we get it. You don't like the fact that Uplay is required to play their games. It is the same thing with Origin. I know there have been issues with game launches, and honestly that is par for the course these days with ANY game release.

The last time I remember games were not having issues is when the SNES was the main console and PC gaming was still in its infancy.

That being said I constantly see on here as well as review sites, such as Metacritic, where people are bashing every Ubisoft that comes out, regardless of if they have played, simply because it is the cool thing to do. You get quick comment points and quick likes on review sites just for saying, "It 2016 Ubisoft, get with the program". My personal favorite is, "I played for 15 minutes and was bored.". How in the world can you get an honest idea of a game from just 15 minutes of gameplay?

Far Cry Primal was bashed because of what I consider, "Mythological game breaking frame rate issues". I didn't experience this at all.

The Division had issues at launch, not because of Ubisoft, but Nvidia put out bad drivers. Who downloads brand new drivers anyways? (Hint turns off auto-updating of your drivers) Buddy with an R9 390 AMD card didn't have any issues past the first day, (fell through the world 3 different times) As far as an MMO type game launch it has been pretty damn flawless. After 79 hours of gameplay, I can attest that I have had better stability than any WoW patch / Expansion. I have had a few crashes, but nothing like my previous MMO experiences. The VOIP Ip issue was the only thing I have seen that is a real issue. That can be solved by using a VPN, yes they shouldn't have made that visible in game, but at this point in time, you really should use a VPN when online.

I would recommend both Far Cry Primal and The Division. Both have been great games, at least in my opinion.

So what gives? If I used the same logic in regards to say, Blizzard, then I would never play any of their games. WoW's history of launch issues speaks for itself.
